audit.whatIsWrong: Every tracked-cooldown reference on the page named 'Repeating Dashes', an ability Ambessa does not have. Her real kit is Drakehound's Step (P), Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam (Q), Repudiation (W), Lacerate (E), Public Execution (R). Separately, the two decisive interactions were both absent.
audit.why: packet.defects: 'never names any of Ambessa's abilities'. The decisive interactions from the kits: Repudiation grants her a shield, and Renekton's Ruthless Predator above 50 Fury destroys damage shields on the target while stunning 1.5s instead of 0.75s. And Public Execution suppresses on arrival then stuns — suppression is the one lockdown Fury cannot buy an escape from, which the mirror audit reached independently.
audit.corrected: The invented name replaced with Public Execution across focus, tldr, winCon, enemyWin, loading, ahead, the breakdown block, the dos, and reports 1/3/5/9/10/12/13. spikes[0].text now states the shield destruction and the 1.5s stun; wants.foe[0] states her braced-shield counterplay; dontsFull[1].d gives the Drakehound's Step auto-reset tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was framed as 'Dominus stats turn even fights into wins', with no number attached to either ultimate.
audit.why: Public Execution is 130/115/100s; Dominus is 120/100/80s. Hers is the longer timer and the harder lockdown, which is why the packet gives level 6 onward to Ambessa.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now carries the 130s figure and the bait-then-answer sequence; phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten to match the corrected chart.

notes: 'Repeating Dashes' was a fabricated ability name occupying every tracked-cooldown slot on this page; it is replaced with Public Execution throughout. The level chart on disk disagreed with the packet at six of seven rows in both layers — flipped as one atomic group. The mirror audit skipped those flips on the belief that enum edits fail the length band; they do not, so this side now carries the packet chart and mirror-fix should reconcile toward it. Repudiation and Public Execution both carry derived 'grounding' flags that Riot's descriptions do not support (shield-and-slam, and blink-suppress-stun respectively) — no grounding claim was made from either. Pronoun gender was corrected to 'her' only inside strings already being edited; several untouched strings still say 'him'.
